intro: I’m Abinav, a data engineer with 2.5+ years of professional experience at Virtusa for BMO. I build Python and SQL batch pipelines processing 5M+ financial records daily with a 99.9% success rate, using Airflow and AWS to deliver reliable reporting data and improve warehouse performance.
whyCompany: Walmart’s data engineering roles connect large-scale pipelines to analytical datasets that business teams can trust. Their recurring focus on SQL, cloud warehouses, data quality and performance matches the work I do in financial data engineering: delivering reporting data, managing dependencies and keeping batch workflows dependable.

The opportunity to contribute to those problems at Walmart’s scale is what draws me here. I bring production Python, SQL, Airflow and AWS experience, alongside hands-on PySpark, Snowflake and dbt work in my personal Retail Sales Lakehouse. That gives me a concrete foundation for contributing to batch processing and analytical models while developing deeper Spark expertise.

canHelp.title: Scalable batch pipelines
canHelp.body: Walmart’s pipeline roles need repeatable ingestion and dependable downstream delivery. At Virtusa for BMO, I built and maintained Python/SQL ETL using Glue, S3 and Airflow, including incremental loads and dependencies across 150+ daily production runs. I would bring that experience to batch workflows serving analytical datasets.

canHelp.title: PySpark processing · Personal project
canHelp.body: Walmart’s Spark-focused roles turn raw data into usable analytical datasets. In my personal lakehouse, I used PySpark for window-based deduplication, schema enforcement, enrichment and row-level rejects, with partitioned Parquet and idempotent batch processing. This is hands-on project evidence, separate from my production AWS work.

canHelp.title: Data quality and production recovery
canHelp.body: Reliable datasets require checks and a clear recovery path. My automated schema, date, missing-column and duplicate validation reduced recurring issues by 25%. I also use CloudWatch, investigate upstream and Glue/Redshift failures, and execute controlled reruns; since June 2026, I’ve held offshore L3 support ownership.

canHelp.title: Warehouse performance and useful models
canHelp.body: Walmart’s warehouse roles emphasize efficient queries and analytics-ready models. My layered Redshift raw-to-reporting models delivered 40% faster queries, and tuned COPY loads were 3× faster than row-level inserts. Separately, my personal project uses dbt dimensions, facts and tests to create trustworthy analytical datasets.

projects.title: Retail Sales Lakehouse
projects.description: A personal batch lakehouse processing 500K+ records across six PostgreSQL entities, plus API ingestion. Airflow coordinates six parallel Bronze jobs and PySpark Silver transformations with window-based deduplication, schema enforcement, FX enrichment and row-level rejects. Transactional watermarks support incremental loads; batch-date partitioned Parquet and runtime parameters make processing repeatable and idempotent. Snowflake stages and COPY INTO feed dbt staging, dimensions, facts and analytical models, validated with unique, not-null and relationship tests.

about: I’m a Data Engineer building scalable data pipelines and warehouse workflows for BMO’s financial data platform at Virtusa. I design production ETL workflows using Python, SQL, Airflow, AWS Glue, S3, and Redshift, processing 5M+ financial records daily. My work focuses on reliable ingestion, data quality, warehouse performance, and production recovery.
